newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended up on Monday on a technical rebound helped by short-covering from retail investors, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 3,376 yuan ($407) per tonne, rising 22 yuan. It opened at 3,370 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,399 and a low of 3,368.
July rose 28 to 3,398, September 30 to 3,410 and November 25 to 3,420. Combined volume fell to 11,600 tonnes from 28,800.
Soybeans opened higher and moved at those levels for most of the session.
Traders said the day's rise was a technical rebound after continuous falls over the past few days.
"Speculative short-covering from retail investors pushed the contracts up, but today's rise in open interest indicated investors were still mixed about short term market trends," one trader said.
"Sharp falls are unlikely in the long term with fundamentals improved, while a lack of strong buying is preventing soybeans from rising sharply," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around current levels in the next few days. ($1=8.2956 yuan)
